prompt_text: Who is the best healthcare marketing agency in St. Louis?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” agency—best depends on your goals, budget, audience and the services you need. I can help find the right fit. A few quick questions will let me give a useful recommendation:

- What type of healthcare client are you? (hospital system, clinic, private practice, medical device, pharma, telehealth, payer, other)
- What services do you need? (branding, digital marketing, content, SEO, paid media, PR, creative, patient acquisition, provider recruitment, analytics)
- Budget range and timeline?
- Do HIPAA/healthcare compliance experience and clinical/medical content expertise matter?
- Do you prefer a local agency only or are remote/national firms OK?

If you’d like to evaluate agencies yourself, use this checklist:
- Relevant experience: case studies with similar healthcare clients and measurable outcomes
- Compliance knowledge: HIPAA, FDA/pharma/telehealth rules if applicable
- Data & attribution: analytics, tracking, ROI measurement
- Creative and clinical accuracy: healthcare-safe creative and medically accurate content
- Integrated capabilities: strategy + digital + PR + patient experience if you need full-funnel work
- Client references and retention rate
- Team seniority and availability
- Pricing model and transparency

Questions to ask shortlisted agencies:
- Have you worked with organizations like ours? Can you share results?
- How do you measure and report ROI for patient acquisition or provider recruitment?
- Who will be the day-to-day contacts and what’s the team structure?
- How do you handle PHI and clinical review for content?
- What’s the expected timeline to see results for SEO/PPC/brand campaigns?

If you want, I can:
- Recommend 4–6 St. Louis agencies that specialize in healthcare and compare them by the criteria above
- Draft outreach/email templates to contact agencies
- Evaluate proposals if you send them to me

Which would you like me to do next?
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
